pool.title: The game's own reference servers
pool.absent: No reference servers for this application yet. Its operator publishes none, and this machine has not seen it connect to any — so the app cannot tell an outage of the game's servers apart from a path you cannot reach.
pool.unproven_one: {{count}} member has never answered a probe and is not counted — a game's match server answers nothing anyone can send, so its silence proves nothing.
pool.unproven_other: {{count}} members have never answered a probe and are not counted — a game's match server answers nothing anyone can send, so their silence proves nothing.
pool.note: Several addresses belonging to this game, in different places, probed rarely. All of them silent while your baselines are clean is the only evidence that points at the game rather than at your path.

chart.label: Round-trip time over time for every endpoint of {{name}}
chart.note: Time runs from the moment you started watching this application, and the drawing grows to the right. One line per endpoint, each point the slowest round trip in a {{seconds}} s slot — so a spike is never smoothed away, and the line sits above the average beside it. The scale is logarithmic, so 4 ms and 400 ms are both readable; nothing is clipped. A dashed line is the route to an endpoint that answers nothing: the round-trip time to a router on the way there, not to the endpoint itself. A break in a line is probes that did not come back.
chart.failed: The chart could not be drawn ({{reason}}). Every figure it would show is in the list below.

picker.hint: Pick up to {{limit}}. Choosing one monitors the whole application — every process it is running under, and anything it launches. Nothing is read from inside them — only which addresses they talk to.

group.udpHint: The connections a game actually plays over
group.udpEmpty: No match traffic discovered yet — nothing of this kind has been seen leaving this application.
group.udpUnobservable: Match traffic cannot be discovered on this machine: per-process flow events are not running, so these connections are invisible to the app. The note above the applications says what to do about it.
group.tcpHint: Sign-in, launchers, content networks and telemetry — not where the game is played, and still where being blocked stops you playing

badge.egressConflict: Probe may not follow this app's route

passive.heading: This endpoint's own traffic
passive.note: Measured from the traffic itself, without sending anything. Not a round-trip time: nothing here times a request against its answer. How evenly the data arrives is what a player feels as stutter, and it includes whatever cadence the server chose — which is why it is shown beside the route rather than instead of it.
passive.updatesUnknown: Not enough arrivals yet to time them

path.heading: Path to this endpoint
path.note: This endpoint answers nothing we can send, so these figures belong to the deepest router that does answer on the way there. It is not the round-trip time to the server: how much further the server sits is unknown.
path.hopUnknown: No hop on the route is answering

quality.uncorroborated: Only the last hop is off — may be that router, not the path

position.reached: The endpoint answered the trace itself
position.nothingAnswered: No router on the way answered; expiry messages are probably filtered locally
position.insideThisNetwork: The route stops inside your own network
position.insideTheAccessNetwork: The route stops inside your provider's network
position.beforeAnyLongHaulLink: The route stops on public infrastructure, before any long-distance link
position.beyondALongHaulLink: The route stops past a long-distance link

flow.notPermitted: This account may not open a tracing session, so UDP endpoints and traffic counters are missing — TCP endpoints are still found. Adding your account to the local “Performance Log Users” group once, from an elevated prompt, restores them. The app never does this for you.
flow.stopped: The tracing session stopped — something else on this machine took it over. UDP endpoints and traffic counters are missing until it is back; the app is retrying every second.
flow.unavailable: Per-process flow events are unavailable on this system, so UDP endpoints and traffic counters are missing. TCP endpoints are still found.

verdict.label: What the measurements add up to
verdict.notEnoughEvidence: Not enough measured yet to say
verdict.nothingMeasurable: Probes are being filtered — nothing could be measured
verdict.clear: Nothing points at a network-wide problem
verdict.localNetworkOrProvider: Services inside your country are failing too — your connection or your provider
verdict.crossBorderPath: Services inside your country answer and services abroad do not — the path out
verdict.routeToThisApplication: The network is fine and this application's own endpoints are not — the route it takes
verdict.gameServersUnreachable: The game's own reference servers are not answering from here
verdict.gameServersPartlyUnreachable: Part of the game's reference servers are not answering from here

advice.localNetworkOrProvider: Check your own equipment first; if that is fine, the problem is upstream of you and a VPN will not help.
advice.crossBorderPath: A VPN may help, since the failure is on the way out rather than on your own line.
advice.routeToThisApplication: A game accelerator may help: everything else reaches the network normally and this application's traffic does not.
advice.gameServers: Nothing on your side would change this. The addresses that belong to this game are not answering from here.

status.unavailable: The core stopped sending service checks
status.cadence: Each service is checked every {{seconds}} s
status.caveat: These checks say whether this machine can reach each service. A service you cannot reach may be running normally for everyone else.

settings.languageHint: More languages are added as data; no part of the app has to change.
settings.countryHint: Chooses the domestic baseline list. Nothing is detected from the network — this app never asks anyone where you are.
settings.intervalHint: How often each baseline target is probed. Longer intervals leave more of the probe budget for the applications you monitor.
settings.autostartHint: Off unless you turn it on. Reflects what the system reports, not what was requested.
settings.rememberGameServers: Remember the servers your games connect to
settings.rememberGameServersHint: Kept on this machine and sent nowhere. It is what lets the app tell "this game's servers are down" apart from "you cannot reach them". Turning it off deletes what was already remembered.
settings.privacyNote: All measurements stay on this machine. The app sends nothing anywhere except the probes on these lists.
